what: Western Alliance is a commercial bank built around national lending niches: lending to technology and life science companies, to mortgage warehouses, to hotels and to homeowner associations, funded by deposits from those same industries.
customers: Businesses in specialised sectors nationally, plus regional banking in Arizona, Nevada and California.
moat: Specialised lending teams that understand industries other banks will not underwrite, which brings both loans and the deposits those industries carry.
risks: The 2023 regional banking crisis hit it hard because of its concentrated deposit base, and the memory persists
Commercial real estate and hotel lending are meaningful exposures
Free cash flow was negative by $284M as the mortgage business consumed cash
opportunities: 7.7 times earnings with a 27.4% net margin
Revenue grew from $2.0B to $3.5B in four years, faster than almost any bank of its size
Analysts see about 29% upside, with 16 covering the stock
watch: Deposit growth and credit quality in commercial real estate.
